title: GPU preemption & tenant SLA retrospective Q4 2025
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This retrospective analyzes a set of incidents in October–November 2025 where tenant-facing requests experienced repeated model-inference degradation due to aggressive GPU preemption during high-utilization windows. The incidents caused two customers to miss latency SLOs for 3–9 hours and increased token cost by ~18% for a third customer because of forced model fallbacks.

Scope
-----
- Services: inference-gateway, scheduler-service, gpu-pool-manager, tenant-pricing-agent
- Time window: 2025-10-20 to 2025-11-02 (primary incidents)
- Impact: 2 enterprise customers (tiered Dedicated capacity), 1 mid-market customer (hosted)

Timeline (compressed)
--------------------
1. 2025-10-20 03:40 UTC: scheduler-service started a global rebalancing job after region capacity alarms triggered.
2. 2025-10-20 03:42 UTC: gpu-pool-manager issued standing preemption for low-priority tenants to reclaim capacity.
3. 2025-10-20 03:45–06:00 UTC: Multiple long-running requests hit preemption mid-run leading to repeated restarts, token double-minting in logs, and model fallback to smaller variants.
4. 2025-10-20 07:10 UTC: alerting pages escalated to on-call but initial playbook steps did not contain preemption-specific mitigations.
5. 2025-10-21 onward: engineering intervention stabilized pools; follow-up investigation launched.

Key metrics observed
--------------------
| Metric | Baseline | Incident peak | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 95th P90 request latency (hosted) | 180 ms | 720 ms | +300% |
| Dedicated tenant SLA breaches (count) | 0/week | 2 (during incident) | +2 |
| Token duplication / reissued tokens | 0/day | ~1200/day | +1200 |
| GPU utilization (region eu-west-1) | 67% | 93% | +26pp |

Root cause analysis (summary)
-----------------------------
- Primary: scheduler-service global rebalancer used an overly aggressive preemption policy with a 30s grace window and immediate eviction for "best-effort" buckets. The policy did not account for multi-stage KV-cache warmups used by long-running chat sessions, so preempted processes lost large KV caches and forced model fallbacks.
- Secondary: alerting/playbook gaps — the on-call runbook for preemption lacked a clear guideline for temporarily disabling rebalancing or increasing grace windows when SLO-sensitive tenants were detected.
- Tertiary: telemetry blind spots — we did not have a token-duplication metric surfaced on dashboards, so cost impact was discovered only during manual billing anomaly review.

What worked well
----------------
- Canary signals: the Dedicated tenant promoted to the highest priority received auto-fallback to reserved pool, limiting full outage for that customer to <30 minutes.
- Observability: request traces contained GPU node IDs which helped correlate restarts to preemption actions within 11 minutes.

Action items (owners and target dates)
-------------------------------------
1. Short-term: Increase preemption grace window from 30s -> 180s for all regions. Owner: Arjun Patel. Due: 2025-11-20.
2. Short-term: Add a temporary block in scheduler-service to skip global rebalancing if >1 SLA breach detected in last 60 minutes. Owner: Maya Chen. Due: 2025-11-18.
3. Mid-term: Implement KV-cache-preserving suspend/resume flow in gpu-pool-manager to avoid full cache evictions on preemption. Owner: Runtime team (listed on related_pages). Due: 2026-02-28.
4. Mid-term: Add token-duplication and model-fallback-rate metrics to the platform SLI dashboard. Owner: Observability (dashboards). Due: 2025-12-10.
5. Long-term: Revise tenant-priority economic model to incentivize short-running bursts vs long-running chat sessions (pricing/credits analysis). Owner: Product & Pricing. Due: 2026-03-31.

Dashboard and alerting changes (concrete)
----------------------------------------
- New panels to add to the Platform Operations dashboard (platform-ops/gpu-overview):
  * "Preemption events by tenant (1h, 24h)" — count of evictions with tenant tag.
  * "KV cache warmup loss" — percentage of requests that lost KV cache within last 10 minutes.
  * "Model fallback rate" — percentage of requests that fell back to smaller model variant.
  * "Token duplication rate" — duplicated token events / total tokens per hour.
- Alert rule updates:
  1) P0: If >1 SLA breach in 60m OR >100 preemption events for any single tenant in 30m -> page oncall and platform lead.
  2) P1: Model fallback rate > 8% for a tenant for 15m -> trigger slack #platform-ops and create a ticket.
  3) P2: Token duplication rate > 200/hr -> email cost-ops.
- Dashboard thresholds suggestion table:
| Panel | Threshold (default) | Severity |
| Preemption events by tenant (30m) | >50 | P1 |
| Model fallback rate (15m) | >8% | P1 |
| Token duplication rate (1h) | >200 | P2 |

Runbook updates (summary)
-------------------------
1. Add a "GPU preemption incident" section to the platform runbook with the following steps:
   a. Identify impacted tenants via trace -> node -> eviction logs.
   b. Temporarily increase preemption grace window and disable global rebalance.
   c. If tenant is Dedicated and SLA-tiered, migrate active jobs to reserved pool or enable soft-affinity.
   d. If token duplication rate observed, enable deduplication circuit in request-coordinator for affected tenant.
2. Create a checklist and automation to rollback changes after stabilization (grace-window reset, re-enable rebalance).

Operational safety and gating
----------------------------
- Any change to preemption timing must be accompanied by capacity pressure simulation in staging. Add a short A/B test in eu-west-1 with canary tag to evaluate latency/cost tradeoffs for 72h before global rollout.
- RBAC: only Platform Leads and SRE OnCall may trigger global-rebalance-disable.

Retrospective learnings and decisions
------------------------------------
- We decided to adopt a multi-dimensional preemption policy that factors: tenant SLA tier, running-job KV-cache-size estimate, and request-latency sensitivity.
- The scheduler-service will treat long-running chat sessions as "cache-sensitive" and use suspend/resume rather than immediate eviction.
- Observability-first: token duplication and model-fallback metrics are now required for any scheduling/eviction change proposal.

Follow-ups (owners)
-------------------
- Product: finalize short-term pricing nudges for long-running sessions. Owner: Leila Novak. Due: 2026-01-15.
- Runtime: design suspend/resume KV cache API and gRPC contract. Owner: Runtime API team. Due: 2026-02-28.
- Observability: dashboard panels + alert rules (implementation + runbook link). Owner: Dashboards team. Due: 2025-12-10.

Appendix: useful queries and command snippets
--------------------------------------------
- List preemption events (Kusto/TSDB pseudo):
  SELECT timestamp, tenant_id, node_id, eviction_reason FROM gpu_preemptions WHERE timestamp > ago(24h) ORDER BY timestamp DESC

- Deduplication toggle (kubectl exec to request-coordinator):
  kubectl exec -n platform request-coordinator -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/dedup?tenant=<TENANT_ID>&enable=true'

- Example Grafana alert JSON snippet (model fallback rule):
  {
    "title": "Model fallback rate high (15m)",
    "expr": "sum(rate(model_fallback_total[15m])) by (tenant) / sum(rate(request_total[15m])) by (tenant) > 0.08",
    "for": "15m"
  }

- Contact matrix:
  * Platform lead (oncall rotation): @arjun.patel@redwood.com
  * Runtime primary: runtime-team@redwood.com
  * Observability primary: dashboards@redwood.com
